overview: RAGLens leverages Sparse Autoencoders to disentangle LLM internal representations into interpretable features, then applies mutual-information-based feature selection and generalized additive models to accurately detect, explain, and mitigate hallucinations in retrieval-augmented generation.

modules.name: Data Loading and Preprocessing
modules.description: Load RAG hallucination benchmark datasets (RAGTruth, Dolly, AggreFact, TofuEval), parse annotated instances containing query, retrieved context, generated answer, and binary hallucination label, and unify them into a standard data structure for downstream processing.

modules.name: LLM Hidden State Extraction
modules.description: Given a frozen LLM and a target layer index, extract per-token hidden states from the specified layer by performing a forward pass conditioned on the query and retrieved context, producing a sequence of hidden state vectors for the generated answer.

modules.name: SAE Sparse Feature Encoding
modules.description: Encode the per-token hidden states through a pre-trained Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) to obtain token-level sparse feature activations, where only a small subset of features are active at each position, preserving interpretable and monosemantic representations.

modules.name: Instance-level Feature Aggregation via Max Pooling
modules.description: Aggregate token-level sparse feature activations into instance-level representations by applying channel-wise max pooling across all token positions, yielding a single feature vector per generation instance that captures the strongest activation of each feature.

modules.name: Mutual Information Based Feature Selection
modules.description: Compute the mutual information between each pooled SAE feature and the hallucination label using a binning-based estimation method, rank features by their mutual information values, and select the top-K' most informative features to form a compact representation for the detector.

modules.name: GAM Hallucination Detector Training
modules.description: Train a Generalized Additive Model (GAM) implemented as an Explainable Boosting Machine on the selected SAE features to predict the binary hallucination label, learning univariate shape functions for each feature that map feature values to their additive contribution on the logit scale.

modules.name: End-to-end Hallucination Detection Pipeline
modules.description: Orchestrate the complete inference pipeline from input (query, context, generated answer) to hallucination prediction, chaining hidden state extraction, SAE encoding, max pooling, feature selection, and GAM prediction, returning the hallucination probability and binary label.

modules.name: Local Explanation via Sparse Feature Attribution
modules.description: Decompose individual GAM predictions into per-feature contributions, align activated SAE features with their corresponding token positions in the generated text, and highlight the specific text spans (e.g., fabricated numbers, dates, or entities) that are most likely ungrounded.

modules.name: Global Explanation via Feature Semantic Interpretation
modules.description: Summarize the semantic meaning of each selected SAE feature by collecting representative activation cases (top-activated and quantile-distributed samples), using an LLM to distill a natural-language description, and visualizing the learned GAM shape function to show how feature magnitude maps to hallucination risk.

modules.name: Hallucination Mitigation via Multi-level Feedback
modules.description: Generate instance-level feedback (hallucination warning only) and token-level feedback (hallucination warning plus highlighted problematic spans) from RAGLens detection and explanation results, then prompt the original LLM to revise its output using this structured feedback to reduce unfaithfulness.

modules.name: Evaluation Metrics Computation
modules.description: Compute all evaluation metrics used in the paper including AUC-ROC, balanced accuracy, and macro F1 score for hallucination detection, as well as hallucination rate for mitigation assessment, supporting both automatic LLM-judge evaluation and human annotation agreement computation.

modules.name: Baseline Detector Implementations
modules.description: Implement or integrate representative baseline hallucination detectors across three categories: prompting-based (Prompt, ChainPoll, RAGAS, FActScore, FactCC, RefCheck, P(True)), uncertainty-based (SelfCheckGPT, LN-Entropy, Energy, Focus, Perplexity, EigenScore), and internal representation-based (SEP, SAPLMA, ITI, ReDeEP), ensuring fair comparison under the same LLM backbone.

modules.name: Cross-model Generalization Evaluation
modules.description: Train RAGLens detectors using SAE features from multiple LLMs (Llama2-7B/13B, Llama3.2-1B, Llama3.1-8B, Qwen3-0.6B/4B) and evaluate their detection performance on RAG outputs generated by different LLMs, comparing against each model's own chain-of-thought self-judgment baseline.

modules.name: Cross-domain Generalization Evaluation
modules.description: Assess domain transferability by training the RAGLens predictor on one dataset or subtask (e.g., RAGTruth-Summary) and evaluating on other datasets or subtasks (e.g., AggreFact, TofuEval, RAGTruth-QA, RAGTruth-Data2txt), comparing against zero-shot CoT prompting baselines.

modules.name: Ablation Study Framework
modules.description: Implement controlled ablation experiments covering four dimensions: (1) layer-wise SAE feature extraction across the full LLM depth, (2) feature extractor comparison (SAE vs. Transcoder, pre-activation vs. post-activation), (3) feature count sensitivity analysis (varying K' with MI ranking vs. random selection), and (4) predictor architecture comparison (LR, GAM, MLP, XGBoost).

modules.name: Interpretability Validation via Counterfactual Perturbation
modules.description: Validate the specificity of identified SAE features to RAG hallucination patterns by conducting counterfactual interventions on the retrieved context (making the output consistent, introducing different inconsistencies, or removing the context entirely) and observing changes in feature activations, alongside causal intervention experiments that manipulate feature values to steer generation behavior.

modules.name: Configuration, Logging, and Experiment Management
modules.description: Manage experiment configurations including LLM backbone selection, SAE layer and architecture settings, feature selection parameters, and GAM hyperparameters; log training and evaluation metrics; support checkpoint saving and loading for the GAM detector; and aggregate results into standardized tables and visualizations for reporting.
